input.note:
**Root Cause:** The 4.3 deployment added `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` to the container's security context as part of the quarterly platform review. Next.js 14 attempts to create the directory `/app/.next/cache` at startup for its image optimizer cache. With a read-only root filesystem, this `mkdir` call fails with `EROFS: read-only file system`, the process exits with code 1, and Kubernetes enters CrashLoopBackOff [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#container-restarts-1].

**Evidence:**
- Pod `docs-site-5c7b9d8f6-wk4pz` (image `docs-site:4.3.0`) has `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` in its security context — absent on the healthy 4.2 pods.
- Pod logs show the exact failure: `Error: EROFS: read-only file system, mkdir '/app/.next/cache'` at `ImageOptimizerCache.init`.
- Pod has 11 restarts, status `CrashLoopBackOff`, last terminated with exit code 1.
- The New Relic 401 error in the logs is a separate/pre-existing issue; the app explicitly continues without APM and is not the crash trigger.

**Fix (apply to the `docs-site` Deployment in the `marketing` namespace):**

Add an `emptyDir` volume and mount it at `/app/.next/cache` so Next.js has a writable scratch location while keeping `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` [cite: concepts/storage/volumes#emptydir-0] [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/security-context#intro-2]:

```yaml
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      volumes:
        - name: nextjs-cache
          emptyDir: {}
      containers:
        - name: docs-site
          # ... existing fields ...
          volumeMounts:
            - name: nextjs-cache
              mountPath: /app/.next/cache
```

Run `kubectl rollout status deployment/docs-site -n marketing` after applying to confirm the 4.3 pods come up healthy. Note that `emptyDir` data is ephemeral and will be cleared on pod restart, which is acceptable for a Next.js image-optimization cache [cite: concepts/storage/volumes#emptydir-0].
